title: WeightBench: Evaluating Language Models as Weight-Space Programmers
abstract: arXiv:2611.18553v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Recent work shows that large language models (LLMs) can operate directly on the parameters of other neural networks. They can read what a network was trained to do, fix a network that fails, and write working networks from scratch, all without gradient descent. This capability has been termed Weight-Space Programming (WSP). Exploring this new paradigm systematically requires a robust benchmark. We introduce WEIGHTBENCH, a benchmark that evaluates LLMs of increasing capability on 42 WSP tasks across five tracks: reading, fixing and writing weights, recognizing edits that are impossible, and data-free compression. The networks whose weights the LLMs read and edit range from 2K-parameter control policies to 7B-parameter language models. translated_title: WeightBench：将语言模型作为权重空间程序员进行评估
translated_abstract: 最近的研究表明，大型语言模型（LLM）可以直接操作其他神经网络的参数。它们能够读取一个网络被训练来做什么，修复失效的网络，并从零开始编写可正常工作的网络——所有这些都无需梯度下降。这种能力被称为权重空间编程。要系统地探索这一新范式，需要一个稳健的基准。我们提出了WEIGHTBENCH，这是一个在五大赛道（读取权重、修复权重、编写权重、识别不可能的编辑以及无数据压缩）上，对能力递增的LLM进行42项WSP任务评估的基准。LLM读取和编辑权重的网络规模从2K参数的控制策略到7B参数的语言模型不等。实验基准结果表明，前沿智能体已经能够读取小型网络并在从未实际运行它们的情况下编写出可正常工作的控制策略，但目前还无法修补语言模型或对其进行压缩。
tldr: 该论文提出了WEIGHTBENCH基准，通过五大赛道的42项权重空间编程任务系统评估语言模型直接读取、修复和编写神经网络参数的能力，发现前沿模型已能读取小型网络并编写可用的控制策略，但尚无法修补或压缩大型语言模型。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces WEIGHTBENCH, a benchmark with 42 weight-space programming tasks across five tracks to systematically evaluate LLMs' ability to directly read, fix, and write neural network parameters, finding that frontier models can already read small networks and write working control policies but cannot yet patch or compress language models.
